item.title: House Takes up Hegseth Impeachment Procedural Vote
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, New York Republican Congressman Nick LaLota reacts to Jim Jordan’s election as incoming House minority leader, while praising Steve Scalise’s record and political skills. Arizona Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego, a Marine Corps combat veteran who served in Iraq, says what he describes as efforts to sidestep Congress on war powers provide “good grounds” for Pete Hegseth’s impeachment, while saying he would review the evidence before any Senate trial. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Anthropic Targets $1.4 Trillion Valuation
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Anthropic is seeking a valuation of about $1.4 trillion in its initial public offering, a bid to make history as the first frontier artificial intelligence lab to go public. The Claude chatbot maker and its co-founders are looking to raise as much as $90.4 billion in the IPO and a private placement. The base offering would raise up to $64.4 billion, with shares marketed for $70 to $78 each, according to a filing on Tuesday with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Anthropic is offering 801.4 million shares, while backers are selling 23.6 million shares.
On today’s episode:
Anthony Hughes, Bloomberg News Equity Capital Market Reporter Matthew Luzzetti, Chief US Economist, Deutsche Bank Dave Lee, Bloomberg Opinion Columnist Melissa Smith, President & CEO, Wex (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sen. Gallego Sees ‘Good Grounds’ for Hegseth Impeachment
item.description: Arizona Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego, a Marine Corps combat veteran who served in Iraq, says what he describes as efforts to sidestep Congress on war powers provide “good grounds” for Pete Hegseth’s impeachment, while saying he would review the evidence before any Senate trial. Sen. Gallego also calls for scrutiny of whether outside influence played a role in Nvidia’s push to loosen chip export controls on China, and says the crypto industry will have to talk to returning Sen. Sherrod Brown and “ask for some forgiveness” after spending heavily against him. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Capitol Hill on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kennedy Family Seeks to Intervene in Fight to Block Trump Arch
item.description: Members of the Kennedy family are seeking to intervene in the legal fight to block construction of a triumphal arch in Washington championed by President Donald Trump, saying it would interfere with memorial gravesites of family members — including JFK’s eternal flame.
item.dc:creator: Jimmy Jenkins

item.title: Rep. LaLota ‘Bullish’ on Bipartisan Lame-Duck Deals
item.description: New York Republican Congressman Nick LaLota reacts to Jim Jordan’s election as incoming House minority leader, while praising Steve Scalise’s record and political skills. Rep. LaLota says he’s confident Republicans can work with Democrats on affordability and other shared priorities, and says he’s “bullish” Congress can use the lame-duck session to make progress on government funding and other bipartisan legislation. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Capitol Hill on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democratic Senators Show Signs of Discontent With Schumer
item.description: Democratic-aligned senators across the ideological spectrum expressed discontent with party Senate leader Chuck Schumer on Tuesday as their sweeping midterm victories ignited calls for bold action.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly and Emily Birnbaum

item.title: Trump’s $10 Billion Suit Against BBC Beats Dismissal Attempt
item.description: A federal judge in Florida ruled that President Donald Trump’s $10 billion lawsuit against British Broadcasting Corp. can proceed, giving a boost to his campaign of litigation against the media.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson

item.title: House Republicans Thwart Massie’s Effort to Impeach Hegseth
item.description: House Republicans blocked the impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for US military actions in the Middle East and Latin America, effectively killing the effort until Democrats take over Congress in January.
item.dc:creator: Roxana Tiron and Erik Wasson

item.title: Hot Inflation, AI Selloff & Anthropic IPO
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Goldman Sachs Asset Management Chief Investment Strategist for Innovator Tim Urbanowicz, Moody’s Chief Credit Officer Atsi Sheth, OpenTable CEO Debby Soo, KPMG Chief Economist Diane Swonk, Texas Capital Bancshares Chairman, President & CEO Rob Holmes, AlphaSimplex Chief Research Strategist & Portfolio Manager Katy Kaminski, D.A. Davidson Technology Research Head Gil Luria, Founder ETFs CIO Lauren Cassidy, Stifel CEO & Chairman Ron Kruszewski, LS Power CEO Paul Segal, & Walker & Dunlop Chairman & CEO Willy Walker. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Texas Capital CEO Rob Holmes on Changing Ticker to TXCP
item.description: Texas Capital has retired its TCBI ticker and adopted TXCP, which Rob Holmes, chairman, president, and CEO of Texas Capital Bank Shares, said reflects the company’s Texas Capital brand and its evolution beyond banking. Holmes described a six-year transformation that created what he called the first full-service financial services firm in Texas. Holmes speaks with Vonnie Quinn & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Targets $1.4 Trillion Valuation
item.description: Anthropic is seeking a valuation of about $1.4 trillion in its initial public offering, a bid to make history as the first frontier artificial intelligence lab to go public. Bailey Lipschultz, Bloomberg News Senior IPO Reporter discusses the IPO valuation targets. Additionally, CPI data came in hot today, reigniting a rate hike debate. Matthew Luzzetti, Chief US Economist at Deutsche Bank discusses what to expect from the Fed. Finally, Dave Lee, Bloomberg Opinion Columnist discusses the latest news on Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged spy. And, Melissa Smith, President & CEO, talks about the latest Wex index and what that means for fleets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ExxonMobil CEO to Miss UN Climate Talks After Three Years
item.description: The chief executive of ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. is ending his streak of attending United Nations climate conferences.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Hegseth Says Massie Bid Hurts Troops
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Kailey Leinz and Tyler Kendall discuss the latest from Capitol Hill. On today’s show, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Rep. Troy Downing (R-MT) and former National Economic Council Director Lael Brainard. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Big Take: Democrats Now Control the Future of the Supreme Court
item.description: Democrats were considering radical reform to address the Supreme Court’s conservative lean. Their sweeping midterms victory changed the conversation. Bloomberg Opinion's Noah Feldman joins David Gura on the Big Take podcast to explain. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Venezuela Passes Power Law to Spur Investment in Ailing Grid
item.description: Venezuelan lawmakers approved a bill designed to attract private investment to the nation’s blackout-prone power grid.
item.dc:creator: Fabiola Zerpa

item.title: Democrats’ Midterms Win Will Allow Them to Reshape SCOTUS Without Court Reform

item.title: Congress Taking Closer Look at Nvidia's Huang
item.description: Top lawmakers in the US House want to hear directly from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang about his relationship with Megaspeed's Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy. Brian Mast, chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told ABC he may subpoena the Nvidia CEO. Bloomberg's Megan Scully reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia CEO Faces Bipartisan Scrutiny Over Affair Probe
item.description: Dave Lee, Bloomberg Opinion columnist, said that lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are poised to investigate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang about his affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. Lee also commented on a New York Times report that reveals President Trump had been told before his trip to China about the concerns around Huang's affair and the fact that his girlfriend was suspected of being a spy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Grocery Prices Rise Again With Little Relief in Sight
item.description: The latest increases partly reflect higher energy costs filtering through the economy.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Sparshott

item.title: Burnham Rejects EU Financial Rules, Shows Brexit Reset Limit
item.description: Andy Burnham’s government won’t accept so-called dynamic alignment of the UK’s financial services rules with those of the European Union, a stance that raises questions about the premier’s wider ambitions for closer ties.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham and Alberto Nardelli
